blocks.text: Practice long questions for the whole of Unit 14 (Vectors in Space), in the shape of a Board Section-II question part: each carries 5 marks (a longer problem, a proof or a derivation). Each one is solved in full, step by step.

blocks.prompt: 1 Let \(\underline{u} = 2\underline{i} - \underline{j} + 3\underline{k}\), \(\underline{v} = \underline{i} + 2\underline{j} - 2\underline{k}\) and \(\underline{w} = 3\underline{i} + \underline{k}\). Find (i) \(|2\underline{u} - \underline{v} + \underline{w}|\) (ii) a unit vector parallel to \(\underline{u} + \underline{v} + \underline{w}\). (5 marks)
blocks.explanation: Build each vector component by component first, then take its magnitude; a unit vector is the vector divided by its own magnitude.

book_ref.quote: We define the magnitude, norm, or length of a vector

blocks.prompt: 2 Prove that \(a(\underline{v} + \underline{w}) = a\underline{v} + a\underline{w}\) for any vectors \(\underline{v}, \underline{w}\) in \(R^{3}\) and \(a \in R\). Verify it for \(a = 3\), \(\underline{v} = [1, -2, 4]\), \(\underline{w} = [2, 0, -1]\). (5 marks)
blocks.explanation: Write the vectors in components and use the distributive law of real numbers in each component.

book_ref.quote: The proofs of the other parts are left as an exercise for the students.

steps: Let \(\underline{v} = [x', y', z']\), \(\underline{w} = [x'', y'', z'']\). Then \(a(\underline{v} + \underline{w}) = a[x' + x'',\ y' + y'',\ z' + z'']\)
\(= [ax', ay', az'] + [ax'', ay'', az''] = a\underline{v} + a\underline{w}\)
blocks.final_answer: Hence proved: \(a(\underline{v} + \underline{w}) = a\underline{v} + a\underline{w}\); for the given data both sides equal \([9, -6, 9]\).

blocks.prompt: 3 Prove that the direction cosines of a non-zero vector satisfy \(\cos^{2}\alpha + \cos^{2}\beta + \cos^{2}\gamma = 1\). Find the direction cosines of \(\overrightarrow{PQ}\) for \(P(2, -1, 3)\), \(Q(4, 1, 2)\) and verify the result. (5 marks)
blocks.explanation: Use the right triangles OAP, OBP, OCP to get each cosine as a component divided by the length.

book_ref.quote: Prove that \(\cos^{2}\alpha + \cos^{2}\beta + \cos^{2}\gamma = 1\).

steps: Let \(\underline{r} = x\underline{i} + y\underline{j} + z\underline{k}\), \(r = |\underline{r}| = \sqrt{x^{2} + y^{2} + z^{2}}\)
In right triangle \(OAP\) (\(A(x, 0, 0)\), right angle at \(A\)): \(\cos\alpha = \frac{x}{r}\); similarly \(\cos\beta = \frac{y}{r}\), \(\cos\gamma = \frac{z}{r}\)
blocks.final_answer: Hence proved: \(\cos^{2}\alpha + \cos^{2}\beta + \cos^{2}\gamma = 1\); for \(\overrightarrow{PQ}\) the direction cosines are \(\frac{2}{3}, \frac{2}{3}, -\frac{1}{3}\).

blocks.prompt: 4 Show that the projection of \(\underline{v}\) along \(\underline{u}\) is \(\dfrac{\underline{u} \cdot \underline{v}}{|\underline{u}|}\). Hence find the projection of \(\underline{v} = 3\underline{i} - 6\underline{j} + 2\underline{k}\) along \(\underline{u} = 2\underline{i} + \underline{j} - 2\underline{k}\) and of \(\underline{u}\) along \(\underline{v}\). (5 marks)
blocks.explanation: Drop a perpendicular from the tip of v to u; OM = |v| cos θ, then replace cos θ from the dot product.

book_ref.quote: Then \(\overline{OM}\) is called the projection of

steps: Projection of \(\underline{v}\) along \(\underline{u}\) \(= \frac{-4}{3}\); projection of \(\underline{u}\) along \(\underline{v}\) \(= \frac{-4}{7}\)
blocks.final_answer: Hence proved: projection of \(\underline{v}\) along \(\underline{u}\) \(= \dfrac{\underline{u} \cdot \underline{v}}{|\underline{u}|}\). Here: \(-\frac{4}{3}\) and \(-\frac{4}{7}\) (negative because the angle is obtuse).

blocks.prompt: 5 Prove that \((\underline{u} + \underline{v}) \cdot (\underline{u} - \underline{v}) = |\underline{u}|^{2} - |\underline{v}|^{2}\). Deduce that the diagonals of a rhombus are perpendicular. (5 marks)
blocks.explanation: Expand with the distributive and commutative properties; in a rhombus the adjacent sides u and v have equal length and the diagonals are u + v and u - v.

book_ref.quote: be vectors and let \(c\) be any real number, then

steps: \((\underline{u} + \underline{v}) \cdot (\underline{u} - \underline{v}) = |\underline{u}|^{2} - |\underline{v}|^{2} = 0\), and both diagonals are non-zero, so they are perpendicular
blocks.final_answer: Hence proved: \((\underline{u} + \underline{v}) \cdot (\underline{u} - \underline{v}) = |\underline{u}|^{2} - |\underline{v}|^{2}\), and the diagonals of a rhombus are perpendicular.

blocks.prompt: 6 If \(\underline{u} = a_{1}\underline{i} + b_{1}\underline{j} + c_{1}\underline{k}\) and \(\underline{v} = a_{2}\underline{i} + b_{2}\underline{j} + c_{2}\underline{k}\), prove that \(\underline{u} \cdot \underline{v} = a_{1}a_{2} + b_{1}b_{2} + c_{1}c_{2}\). Use it to find \(\underline{u} \cdot \underline{v}\) for \(\underline{u} = 2\underline{i} - 5\underline{j} + \underline{k}\), \(\underline{v} = 3\underline{i} + \underline{j} - 4\underline{k}\). (5 marks)
blocks.explanation: Expand by the distributive law into nine terms and use the dot products of the unit vectors.

book_ref.quote: From distributive law we can write:

steps: \(= a_{1}a_{2}(\underline{i} \cdot \underline{i}) + a_{1}b_{2}(\underline{i} \cdot \underline{j}) + a_{1}c_{2}(\underline{i} \cdot \underline{k}) + b_{1}a_{2}(\underline{j} \cdot \underline{i}) + b_{1}b_{2}(\underline{j} \cdot \underline{j}) + b_{1}c_{2}(\underline{j} \cdot \underline{k}) + c_{1}a_{2}(\underline{k} \cdot \underline{i}) + c_{1}b_{2}(\underline{k} \cdot \underline{j}) + c_{1}c_{2}(\underline{k} \cdot \underline{k})\)
blocks.final_answer: Hence proved: \(\underline{u} \cdot \underline{v} = a_{1}a_{2} + b_{1}b_{2} + c_{1}c_{2}\); for the given vectors \(\underline{u} \cdot \underline{v} = -3\).

blocks.prompt: 7 Let \(\underline{u} = 2\underline{i} + \alpha\underline{j} + \underline{k}\) and \(\underline{v} = \underline{i} - 2\underline{j} + 3\underline{k}\). (i) Find \(\alpha\) so that \(\underline{u}\) and \(\underline{v}\) are perpendicular. (ii) For \(\alpha = 1\), find the angle between \(\underline{u}\) and \(\underline{v}\). (5 marks)
blocks.explanation: Perpendicular means dot product zero; the angle comes from cos θ = (u·v)/(|u||v|).

book_ref.quote: The angle between two vectors \(\underline{u}\) and \(\underline{v}\) is determined from the definition of dot product

blocks.prompt: 8 Show that the points \(A(1, 0, 2)\), \(B(3, 1, 1)\) and \(C(2, -1, 3)\) are the vertices of a right triangle. Find its area. (5 marks)
blocks.explanation: Find the side vectors; a zero dot product at one vertex gives the right angle; check with Pythagoras.

book_ref.quote: The angle between two vectors \(\underline{u}\) and \(\underline{v}\) is determined from the definition of dot product

blocks.final_answer: Right triangle with the right angle at \(A\); area \(= \frac{3\sqrt{2}}{2}\) square units.

blocks.explanation: Add the forces to get the resultant, find the displacement AB, then W = F · d.

blocks.prompt: 11 If \(\underline{u} = a_1\underline{i} + b_1\underline{j} + c_1\underline{k}\) and \(\underline{v} = a_2\underline{i} + b_2\underline{j} + c_2\underline{k}\), derive the determinant formula \(\underline{u} \times \underline{v} = \begin{vmatrix} \underline{i} & \underline{j} & \underline{k} \\ a_1 & b_1 & c_1 \\ a_2 & b_2 & c_2 \end{vmatrix}\). (5 marks)
blocks.explanation: Expand by the distributive property and replace each unit-vector cross product by its value.

book_ref.quote: which is known as determinant formula for

steps: \(\underline{u} \times \underline{v} = a_1a_2(\underline{i} \times \underline{i}) + a_1b_2(\underline{i} \times \underline{j}) + a_1c_2(\underline{i} \times \underline{k}) + b_1a_2(\underline{j} \times \underline{i}) + b_1b_2(\underline{j} \times \underline{j}) + b_1c_2(\underline{j} \times \underline{k}) + c_1a_2(\underline{k} \times \underline{i}) + c_1b_2(\underline{k} \times \underline{j}) + c_1c_2(\underline{k} \times \underline{k})\)
\(= a_1b_2\underline{k} - a_1c_2\underline{j} - b_1a_2\underline{k} + b_1c_2\underline{i} + c_1a_2\underline{j} - c_1b_2\underline{i}\)
This is the expansion of \(\begin{vmatrix} \underline{i} & \underline{j} & \underline{k} \\ a_1 & b_1 & c_1 \\ a_2 & b_2 & c_2 \end{vmatrix}\) along the first row
blocks.final_answer: Hence proved: \(\underline{u} \times \underline{v} = \begin{vmatrix} \underline{i} & \underline{j} & \underline{k} \\ a_1 & b_1 & c_1 \\ a_2 & b_2 & c_2 \end{vmatrix}\).

blocks.prompt: 12 For \(\underline{a} = 3\underline{i} + \underline{j} - 2\underline{k}\) and \(\underline{b} = \underline{i} - \underline{j} + 2\underline{k}\), find \(\underline{a} \times \underline{b}\) and \(\underline{b} \times \underline{a}\), show that \(\underline{a} \times \underline{b}\) is perpendicular to both \(\underline{a}\) and \(\underline{b}\), and find a unit vector perpendicular to both and the sine of the angle between \(\underline{a}\) and \(\underline{b}\). (5 marks)
blocks.explanation: Use the determinant formula; the perpendicular check is two dot products; the sine comes from |a × b|/(|a||b|).

blocks.prompt: 13 Prove that \(|\underline{u} \times \underline{v}|^{2} + (\underline{u} \cdot \underline{v})^{2} = |\underline{u}|^{2}|\underline{v}|^{2}\). Verify it for \(\underline{u} = \underline{i} + \underline{j}\), \(\underline{v} = \underline{j} + \underline{k}\). (5 marks)
blocks.explanation: Write both products in terms of the same angle and use sin² θ + cos² θ = 1.

book_ref.quote: is determined from the definition of cross product.

blocks.final_answer: Hence proved: \(|\underline{u} \times \underline{v}|^{2} + (\underline{u} \cdot \underline{v})^{2} = |\underline{u}|^{2}|\underline{v}|^{2}\); for the given vectors \(3 + 1 = 4\).

blocks.prompt: 14 Find the area of the triangle with vertices \(A(2, 1, 0)\), \(B(3, -1, 2)\) and \(C(0, 2, 1)\), and a unit vector perpendicular to its plane. (5 marks)
blocks.explanation: Take two sides from the same vertex; half the magnitude of their cross product is the area; the cross product divided by its magnitude is the unit normal.

blocks.explanation: Opposite sides equal as vectors means a parallelogram; its area is the magnitude of the cross product of two adjacent sides.

steps: Hence \(AB\) and \(DC\) are equal and parallel: \(ABCD\) is a parallelogram
blocks.final_answer: \(ABCD\) is a parallelogram; area \(= \sqrt{29}\) square units.

blocks.prompt: 17 Show that \((\underline{u} \times \underline{v}) \cdot \underline{w}\) is the volume of the parallelepiped with conterminous edges \(\underline{u}\), \(\underline{v}\), \(\underline{w}\), and that \((\underline{u} \times \underline{v}) \cdot \underline{w} = (\underline{v} \times \underline{w}) \cdot \underline{u} = (\underline{w} \times \underline{u}) \cdot \underline{v}\). (5 marks)
blocks.explanation: Volume = base area × height; the base area is |u × v| and the height is the component of w along u × v.

book_ref.quote: represents the volume of the parallelepiped having

steps: Let \(\theta\) be the angle between \(\underline{u} \times \underline{v}\) and \(\underline{w}\): \((\underline{u} \times \underline{v}) \cdot \underline{w} = |\underline{u} \times \underline{v}||\underline{w}|\cos\theta\)
\(|\underline{u} \times \underline{v}|\) = area of the parallelogram (base) with adjacent sides \(\underline{u}\) and \(\underline{v}\)
\(|\underline{w}|\cos\theta\) = height of the parallelepiped (\(\underline{u} \times \underline{v}\) is perpendicular to the base)
So \((\underline{u} \times \underline{v}) \cdot \underline{w}\) = (area of base)(height) = volume of the parallelepiped

Taking the base on \(\underline{v}, \underline{w}\) or on \(\underline{w}, \underline{u}\) gives the same volume as \((\underline{v} \times \underline{w}) \cdot \underline{u}\) or \((\underline{w} \times \underline{u}) \cdot \underline{v}\)

Find its volume, and its height when the base is formed by \(\underline{u}\) and \(\underline{v}\). (5 marks)
blocks.explanation: Volume = |(u × v) · w| and base area = |u × v|; height = volume ÷ base area.

Find the volume of the tetrahedron with vertices \(A(1, 1, 1)\), \(B(2, 1, 3)\), \(C(3, 2, 1)\), \(D(1, 4, 2)\). (5 marks)
blocks.explanation: Volume = 1/3 (base triangle area)(height); the triangle is half the parallelogram, and parallelogram × height is the parallelepiped volume.

book_ref.quote: Volume of the tetrahedron

steps: \(|\underline{u} \times \underline{v}|(h)\) is the volume of the parallelepiped on \(\underline{u}, \underline{v}, \underline{w}\), that is \((\underline{u} \times \underline{v}) \cdot \underline{w}\)
blocks.final_answer: Hence proved: volume \(= \frac{1}{6}[\underline{u}\ \underline{v}\ \underline{w}]\); here the volume is \(\frac{13}{6}\) cubic units.

blocks.prompt: 20 For \(\underline{u} = a_1\underline{i} + b_1\underline{j} + c_1\underline{k}\), \(\underline{v} = a_2\underline{i} + b_2\underline{j} + c_2\underline{k}\), \(\underline{w} = a_3\underline{i} + b_3\underline{j} + c_3\underline{k}\), prove that \(\underline{u} \cdot (\underline{v} \times \underline{w}) = \begin{vmatrix} a_1 & b_1 & c_1 \\ a_2 & b_2 & c_2 \\ a_3 & b_3 & c_3 \end{vmatrix}\). Evaluate it for \(\underline{u} = 2\underline{i} - 3\underline{j} + \underline{k}\), \(\underline{v} = \underline{i} + 2\underline{j} - \underline{k}\), \(\underline{w} = 3\underline{i} + \underline{j} + 2\underline{k}\). (5 marks)
blocks.explanation: Find v × w by the determinant formula, then dot it with u; the result is the 3×3 determinant expanded along its first row.

book_ref.quote: Which is called the determinant formula for scalar triple product of

steps: \(\underline{u} \cdot (\underline{v} \times \underline{w}) = a_1(b_2c_3 - b_3c_2) - b_1(a_2c_3 - a_3c_2) + c_1(a_2b_3 - a_3b_2)\)
This is \(\begin{vmatrix} a_1 & b_1 & c_1 \\ a_2 & b_2 & c_2 \\ a_3 & b_3 & c_3 \end{vmatrix}\) expanded along the first row
blocks.final_answer: Hence proved: \(\underline{u} \cdot (\underline{v} \times \underline{w})\) equals the determinant of the components; for the given vectors it is \(20\).

blocks.prompt: 21 Prove that the points \(A(1, 0, 2)\), \(B(2, 1, 3)\), \(C(3, 0, 1)\) and \(D(1, 2, 5)\) are coplanar. (5 marks)
blocks.explanation: The four points are coplanar exactly when the three vectors AB, AC, AD are coplanar, i.e. their scalar triple product is zero.

book_ref.quote: Vectors are coplanar if they lie in the same plane

steps: The scalar triple product is zero, so \(\underline{AB}\), \(\underline{AC}\), \(\underline{AD}\) are coplanar

blocks.prompt: 24 A force \(\underline{F} = [10, -20, 5]\) N is applied at the point \(P(3, 1, -2)\). Find the torque about the pivot \(M(1, 0, 1)\) and its magnitude (distances in metres). (5 marks)
blocks.explanation: Torque about M is r × F with r the vector from M to the point of application P.
